aliases: Mass cytometry analysis of human peripheral blood leukocytes from COVID-19 patients
mass cytometry.readouts: immune cell subset frequencies; intracellular signaling marker expression including pS6, IκBα, and HLA-DR

evidence_location.section: Analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes from COVID-19 patients by mass cytometry
evidence_location.quote: There was a notable increase in the frequency of plasmablast and effector CD8 T cells in all infected individuals.

aliases: Flow cytometry analysis of ex vivo stimulated human peripheral blood leukocytes from COVID-19 patients
flow cytometry.readouts: fractions of pDCs, mDCs, and monocytes producing IFN-α, TNF-α, and IL-6 after TLR stimulation; NF-κB p65 phosphorylation; HLA-DR expression

evidence_location.section: COVID-19 results in functional impairment of blood myeloid cells and pDCs
evidence_location.quote: Consistent with our hypothesis, there was reduced production of IFN-α in response to the TLR stimuli in the pDCs of infected individuals compared with those of healthy controls.

aliases: Multiplex analysis of cytokines in the plasma of COVID-19 patients
Olink multiplex inflammation panel.readouts: normalized protein expression levels of cytokines, chemokines, and inflammatory mediators including IL-6, MCP-3, CXCL10, TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and OSM

evidence_location.section: Enhanced concentrations of cytokines and inflammatory mediators in plasma from COVID-19 patients
evidence_location.quote: Of these 71 proteins, 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, were significantly up-regulated in COVID-19 infection.

ELISA.readouts: protein concentrations of TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and OSM

evidence_location.section: Enhanced concentrations of cytokines and inflammatory mediators in plasma from COVID-19 patients
evidence_location.quote: Consistent with the multiplex Olink analysis, we found a significant increase of these inflammatory mediators in the plasma of severe and intensive care unit (ICU) COVID-19 patients.

aliases: cellular indexing of transcriptomes and epitopes by sequencing
CITE-seq.readouts: single-cell gene expression and antibody-derived protein expression; cell clusters; ISG signatures; HLA-DR/CD86 and S100A12-associated myeloid states

evidence_location.section: Single-cell transcriptional response to COVID-19 infection
evidence_location.quote: Notably, with the exception of modest levels of IFN-γ expression in T and NK cells, we could not detect any expression of IFN-α and -β genes, which is consistent with the functional data demonstrating impaired type I IFN production by pDCs and myeloid cells.

evidence_location.section: Single-cell transcriptional response to COVID-19 infection
evidence_location.quote: We observed a marked increase in the concentration of IFN-α, which peaked around day 8 after onset of symptoms and regressed to baseline levels by day 20.

bulk RNA sequencing.readouts: bulk gene expression, including ISG signature and IFN-related transcripts

evidence_location.section: Single-cell transcriptional response to COVID-19 infection
evidence_location.quote: We observed a strong induction of the ISGs in COVID-19 subjects compared with healthy donors in this dataset as well.

PCR quantitation of bacterial 16 S ribos.name_in_paper: PCR quantitation of bacterial 16 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene product
PCR quantitation of bacterial 16 S ribos.readouts: bacterial DNA levels measured via bacterial 16S rRNA gene

evidence_location.section: Severe COVID-19 infection is associated with the systemic release of bacterial products
evidence_location.quote: Notably, the plasma of severe and ICU patients had significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA, as measured by PCR quantitation of bacterial 16 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene product.

evidence_location.section: Severe COVID-19 infection is associated with the systemic release of bacterial products
evidence_location.quote: Notably, the plasma of severe and ICU patients had significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA, as measured by PCR quantitation of bacterial 16 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene product, and of LPS, as measured by a TLR4-based reporter assay.
